finding: During a cTime upgrade of a DataNode with two volumes, volume 1's deferred upgrade callable (executor thread) sets the shared BlockPoolSliceStorage layoutVersion/cTime to the new values while the BP actor thread's doTransition for volume 2 is between readProperties and its version check. Volume 2 then takes the regular-startup path and gets VERSION(cTime=T1) with no previous/ snapshot. A later supported -rollback rejects volume 2 at BlockPoolSliceStorage.doTransition:422 ('Datanode state ... is newer than the namespace state') and the block pool fails to initialize.
same_root_cause: This is the fix's defect. In the buggy DataStorage.loadBlockPoolSliceStorage (DataStorage.java:450-471) each volume's upgrade callables go to executor.submit(c) inside the per-volume loop, while later volumes are still loading through the same bpStorage. The callable runs BlockPoolSliceStorage.doUpgrade (BlockPoolSliceStorage.java:533-537: this.layoutVersion = DATANODE_LAYOUT_VERSION; this.cTime = nsInfo.getCTime()), which races with doTransition's readProperties(sd) (line 389) and its check against this.layoutVersion/this.cTime (lines 405-425) for the next volume. The fix hunk collects the callables in upgradeCallableMap and submits them only after the loop has finished loading every volume, which removes exactly this interleaving.
realistic: Yes. The test uses a MiniDFSCluster, a NameNode -upgrade, a NameNode bounce while the DN starts (the DN's versionRequest fails and is retried), and then an admin -rollback of an un-finalized upgrade. All of these are supported operations. The interleaving comes only from delays: spied NamespaceInfo getters return the real values and just pause the actor thread after volume 2's readProperties, and pause the executor thread before it reads the new cTime. A slow hard-link phase on a big volume can produce this ordering under the real scheduler. The test fabricates no state and makes no direct calls to internal methods.
fixed_version: NOT_REPRODUCED in 2 of 2 runs (rc 0, about 44s each). With the fix the callables are submitted only after volume 2's doTransition. The actor thread's wait therefore times out (30s), and then both volumes are upgraded with previous/ snapshots, so the rollback succeeds and the check no longer fires.
reason: The agent's failing execution comes from the race the fix removes: upgrade callables submitted while other volumes are still loading write the shared layoutVersion/cTime of the one BlockPoolSliceStorage. As a result a later volume is wrongly treated as already upgraded and is later rejected by the doTransition layout/cTime check. The consequence matches the JIRA: a volume is stamped with the new version but has no snapshot, and the DataNode rejects it at the 'is newer than the namespace state' check when rolling back. The JIRA's case is an LV-based variant of the same mechanism, and the agent's is cTime-based. The trigger is realistic, and the fixed version no longer fails.
